duplicate_data_handling.question: Does our model solve duplicate data?
duplicate_data_handling.answer: YES, through a multi-layered deduplication strategy spanning all 4 agents

layers.description: Uses entity_registry dictionary to remove exact duplicates within the same FIR document
layers.evidence: Processed 14 FIR images showing entity extraction

layers.description: BGE-m3 embeddings (1024-dim) + HAC clustering with threshold matrix: ≥0.95 merged (confident duplicates), 0.80-0.95 pending review (manual check), <0.80 separate entities. Includes Metaphone blocking for phonetic pre-filtering.
layers.evidence: BGE-m3 embedder loads, pgvector schema updated with centroid_embedding column, HNSW index created, similarity search method implemented

layers.description: Centroid embeddings stored in PostgreSQL pgvector with HNSW index for O(log n) similarity search. resolve_new_mention() API checks existing clusters before creating new ones.
layers.evidence: Database schema includes centroid_embedding column, similarity search method implemented in ResolutionRepository

layers.description: Neo4j automatically prevents duplicate edges between same node pairs. Multiple evidence for same relationship tracked in edge properties.
layers.evidence: Schema updated with is_predicted flag, Neo4j export capabilities present

layers.description: Results inherently deduplicated by graph structure. Query caching prevents redundant computation via MD5 keys and TTL.
layers.evidence: Natural language interface implemented, query caching with MD5 keys, REST API endpoints defined

duplicate_data_handling.summary: The pipeline handles duplicates at multiple levels: within documents (exact matches), across documents (semantic similarity), incrementally (persistent embeddings), at the graph level (structural constraints), and at the query level (structural + caching). This provides comprehensive deduplication suitable for forensic evidence processing where entities may appear across multiple documents with variations.
